instruction: Center-align the first paragraph of the document.

parameters.window_name: 04 CHIN9505 EBook Purchasing info 2021 Jan.docx - LibreOffice Writer

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to use tabstops to split sentences (first 3 words left, rest right). Successfully navigated Format > Paragraph > Tabs dialog and set a right-aligned tab stop at 15cm. Failed when manually editing each line to insert tabs: text concatenation errors, partial completion, unintended formatting changes.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Writer menus (Format > Paragraph), open dialogs, select all text (Ctrl+A), use toolbar formatting options, type text, use keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at precise text manipulation: inserting tab characters mid-line caused text concatenation, undo didn't fully restore state, and manual line-by-line editing was error-prone. Only completed partial lines with some getting unintended bold/red formatting.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single-step alignment change. Model demonstrated it can click into paragraphs and access alignment tools from the toolbar, so centering one paragraph is within its capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires clicking on the first paragraph and applying center alignment. Getter reads the docx file and extracts the alignment property of the first non-empty paragraph. Metric checks if alignment equals 'center'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts alignment of first non-empty paragraph from docx using python-docx, with proper WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH mapping including None->left default
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_alignment') directly from the rules dict
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state
Single instruction requirement (center-align first paragraph) is fully covered by the evaluator
Data flow is correct: getter returns {'alignment': str} -> metric compares result['alignment'] against expected['expected_alignment'] with case-insensitive comparison
